articles.text: Each worker shall be entitled to a fully paid leave on Eids and occasions specified in the Regulations.

articles.label: Article 113
articles.chapter: Part 6: Work Conditions and Circumstances > Chapter 1: Wages > Chapter 2: Working Hours > Chapter 3: Rest Periods and Weekly Rest Days > Chapter 4: Leaves
articles.text:
Taking into account female workers’ leaves as provided for under this Law, a worker shall be
entitled to a fully paid five-day leave in the event of the worker’s marriage or the death of the
worker’s spouse, ascendant, or descendant from the date such events occur; a fully paid three-
day leave in the event of the death of the worker’s brother or sister from the date such event
occurs; and a fully paid three-day leave in the event of childbirth to be taken within seven days
from the date of the childbirth. In all cases, the employer shall have the right to request
documents proving such events

articles.label: Article 114
articles.chapter: Part 6: Work Conditions and Circumstances > Chapter 1: Wages > Chapter 2: Working Hours > Chapter 3: Rest Periods and Weekly Rest Days > Chapter 4: Leaves
articles.text:
A worker shall be entitled to a paid leave of not less than 10 days and not more than 15 days, including
Eid Al-Adha holiday, to perform Hajj only once during his service if he has not performed it before.
To be eligible for this leave, the worker must have spent at least two consecutive years of service
with the employer. The employer may determine the number of workers who shall be given this leave
annually in accordance with work requirements.

articles.label: Article 115
articles.chapter: Part 6: Work Conditions and Circumstances > Chapter 1: Wages > Chapter 2: Working Hours > Chapter 3: Rest Periods and Weekly Rest Days > Chapter 4: Leaves
articles.text:
1. If an employer approves of a worker’s enrollment or continuance in an educational
institution, he shall have the right to a leave with full pay to sit for an examination for an
unrepeated year, the duration of which shall be based on the actual number of examination
days. If the examination is for a repeat year, the worker shall have the right to a leave without
pay based on the number of actual examination days. Without prejudice to the employer’s
right to disciplinary action, the worker shall be denied the wage if it is established that he
did not sit for the examination.
2. If a worker does not obtain the employer’s approval on his enrollment in an educational
institution, the worker shall be entitled to a leave to sit for the examination based on the
actual number of examination days which shall be considered part of his annual leave, if
available. If this is not possible, the worker shall be entitled to a leave without pay for the
actual number of examination days.
3. The worker shall apply for the leave at least 15 days in advance.
4. The employer may require the worker to submit documents supporting the leave application,
as well as proof of having taken the examination

articles.label: Article 116
articles.chapter: Part 6: Work Conditions and Circumstances > Chapter 1: Wages > Chapter 2: Working Hours > Chapter 3: Rest Periods and Weekly Rest Days > Chapter 4: Leaves
articles.text:
A worker, subject to the employer’s approval, may obtain an unpaid leave for a duration to be agreed
upon by the two parties. The employment contract shall be deemed suspended for the duration of the
leave in excess of 20 days, unless both parties agree otherwise.

articles.label: Article 117
articles.chapter: Part 6: Work Conditions and Circumstances > Chapter 1: Wages > Chapter 2: Working Hours > Chapter 3: Rest Periods and Weekly Rest Days > Chapter 4: Leaves
articles.text:
A worker whose illness has been proven shall be eligible for a paid sick leave for the first 30 days,
three quarters of the wage for the next 60 days, and without pay for the following 30 days, during a
single year, whether such leaves are continuous or intermittent. A single year shall mean the year
which begins from the date of the first sick leave.

articles.label: Article 118
articles.chapter: Part 6: Work Conditions and Circumstances > Chapter 1: Wages > Chapter 2: Working Hours > Chapter 3: Rest Periods and Weekly Rest Days > Chapter 4: Leaves
articles.text:
A worker may not work for another employer, while enjoying any of the leaves provided for in this
Chapter. If the employer proves that the worker has violated this provision, he may deprive him of
his wages for the duration of the leave or recover any wages previously paid to him.

articles.label: Article 119
articles.chapter: Part 7: Part-Time Work
articles.text:
Full-time workers who are affected by a collective temporary reduction in their normal working hours
for economic, technical, or structural reasons shall not be considered part-time workers.

articles.label: Article 120
articles.chapter: Part 7: Part-Time Work
articles.text:
The Minister shall issue the necessary rules and controls for organizing part-time work, indicating
therein the obligations of part-time workers and employers. To the exclusion of the protection
extended to similar full-time workers in terms of occupational health and safety and work injuries,
the provisions of this Law shall apply only to the extent determined by the Minister.
Injuries, and Health and Social Services

articles.label: Article 121
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards
articles.text:
An employer shall maintain the establishment in a clean and hygienic condition. He shall provide
lighting, supply potable and washing water, and comply with other rules, measures, and standards of
occupational protection, health, and safety in accordance with what is specified in the Minister’s
decision.

articles.label: Article 122
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards
articles.text:
An employer shall take the necessary precautions to protect workers against hazards, occupational
diseases, and the machinery in use, and shall ensure work safety and protection. He shall post in a
visible place in the establishment the instructions related to work and workers’ safety in Arabic and,
when necessary, in any other language the workers understand. The employer may not charge the
workers or deduct from their wages any amounts for the provision of such protection.

articles.label: Article 123
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards
articles.text:
An employer shall inform the worker, prior to engaging in the work, of the hazards of his job and
said employer shall require him to use the prescribed protective equipment. The employer shall
supply workers with the appropriate personal protective gear and train them on its use.

articles.label: Article 124
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards
articles.text:
A worker shall use and preserve the personal protective equipment designated for each process and
shall adhere to the instructions established to protect his health against injuries and diseases. He shall
refrain from any action or omission that may lead to failure to implement the instructions, or misuse
or impairment of the devices provided to protect the workplace as well as the health and safety of
fellow workers.

articles.label: Article 125
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards
articles.text:
An employer shall take necessary precautions for protection against fire and provide the technical
means to combat it, including safety exits which shall be maintained in working condition at all times.
He shall post in a visible location in the workplace detailed instructions for fire prevention devices.

articles.label: Article 126
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards
articles.text:
An employer shall be responsible for emergencies and accidents which may affect persons, other than
his workers, who enter the workplace by virtue of their official duties or with the approval of the
employer or his agents, if such emergencies and accidents are due to negligence in taking the technical
precautions required by the nature of his work, and he shall compensate them for damage and harm
they may sustain in accordance with the general laws.

articles.label: Article 127
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents
articles.text: The provisions of this Chapter shall apply to high risk establishments.

articles.label: Article 128
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents
articles.text:
1. The term “high risk establishment” shall mean an establishment which produces, prepares,
disposes of, handles, uses, or stores, on a permanent or temporary basis, one or more hazardous
substances, or categories of these substances, in quantities that exceed permissible limits the
exceeding of which results in listing the establishment among the high risk establishments.
2. The term “hazardous substance” shall mean any substance or mixture of substances that constitutes
a hazard on account of its chemical, physical, or toxic properties either alone or in combination
with other substances.
3. The term “major accident” shall mean any sudden occurrence, such as a major leak, fire, or
explosion in the course of an activity within a high risk establishment and which involves one or
more hazardous substances posing a great immediate or potential danger to the workers, the public,
or the environment.

articles.label: Article 129
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents
articles.text:
The Ministry shall establish controls to identify high risk establishments according to the list of
hazardous substances, their categories, or both.

articles.label: Article 130
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents
articles.text:
Employers shall coordinate with the Ministry to determine the status of their establishments on the
basis of the controls referred to in Article 129 of this Law.

articles.label: Article 131
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents
articles.text:
The Minister shall issue the regulations and decisions that include the necessary arrangements at
establishment level for protection against major hazards, related duties of employers, arrangements
for protecting the public and the environment outside the site of each high risk establishment,
worker’s rights and duties, and other measures necessary to prevent major accidents, minimize the
risks of their occurrence, and mitigate their impacts

articles.label: Article 131 bis
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents
articles.text: The Minister shall, pursuant to a decision issued thereby, determine the professions and jobs that are deemed dangerous or hazardous and are likely to expose the worker to extraordinary risk or harm, and shall determine categories of workers that are permanently or temporary banned from occupying said professions and jobs, or the conditions for occupying said professions and jobs, including the need to set working hours for such categories, in accordance with international agreements to which the Kingdom is a party.

articles.label: Article 132
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries
articles.text:
The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to the establishments subject to the Occupational
Hazards Branch of the Social Insurance Law.

articles.label: Article 133
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries
articles.text:
If a worker sustains a work injury or an occupational disease, the employer shall be required to treat
him and assume, directly or indirectly, all necessary expenses, including hospitalization, medical
examinations and tests, radiology, prosthetic devices, and transportation expenses to treatment
centers.

articles.label: Article 134
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries
articles.text:
An injury shall be deemed a work injury in accordance with the provisions of the Social Insurance
Law. Occupational diseases shall also be considered work injuries and the date of the first medical
diagnosis of the disease shall be treated tantamount to the date of injury.

articles.label: Article 135
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries
articles.text:
Any relapse or complication arising from an injury shall be deemed an injury and shall be treated as
such in terms of aid and treatment.

articles.label: Article 136
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries
articles.text:
Occupational diseases shall be determined in accordance with the Occupational Diseases Schedule
provided for in the Social Insurance Law. Degree of total or partial disability shall be determined
according to the Disability Percentage Guide provided for in said law.

articles.label: Article 137
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries
articles.text:
In the case of temporary disability arising from a work injury, the injured party shall be entitled
to financial aid equal to his full wage for 60 days, then 75% of the wage for the entire duration
of his treatment. If one year elapses, or it is medically determined that the injured party’s
chances of recovery are improbable or that he is not physically fit to work, his injury shall be
deemed a total disability. In this case, the contract shall be terminated and the worker shall be
compensated for the injury. The employer shall not be entitled to recover payments made to the
injured worker during that year

articles.label: Article 138
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries
articles.text:
If an injury results in a permanent total disability or the death of the injured person, the injured person
or his eligible beneficiaries shall be entitled to a compensation equal to his wages for three years,
with a minimum of 54,000 riyals.
If the injury results in a permanent partial disability, the injured person shall be entitled to a
compensation equal to the percentage of the estimated disability in accordance with the approved
Disability Percentage Guide schedule multiplied by the amount of compensation for permanent total
disability.

articles.label: Article 139
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries
articles.text:
An employer shall not be required to comply with the provisions of Articles 133, 137, and 138 of this
Law if any of the following is established:
1. If a worker deliberately injures himself.
2. If an injury is caused by intentional misconduct on the part of the worker.
3. If a worker refuses to be examined by a physician or refuses to accept treatment by the physician
designated by the employer without a valid reason.

articles.label: Article 140
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries
articles.text:
Liability of previous employers of a worker suffering from an occupational disease shall be
determined in light of the medical report of the attending physician. Previous employers shall be
required to pay the compensation provided for in Article 138 of this Law, each in proportion to the
period said worker spent in his service, provided that the industries or occupations they engage in
cause the disease the worker suffers from.

articles.label: Article 141
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries
articles.text: Procedures for reporting work injuries shall be determined pursuant to a decision by the Minister.

articles.label: Article 142
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries > Chapter 4: Medical and Social Services
articles.text:
An employer shall make available one or more medical aid cabinets, supplied with drugs and other
necessities required for first aid.
The Regulations shall specify the contents of such cabinets of first aid means, and the number of such
means and quantities of drugs, and shall also regulate the method of keeping them and the conditions
and requirements to be met by first aid providers.

articles.label: Article 143
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries > Chapter 4: Medical and Social Services
articles.text:
An employer shall assign one or more physicians to provide, at least once a year, a comprehensive
medical examination for his workers who are exposed to any of the occupational diseases listed in
the Schedules of Occupational Diseases provided for in the Social Insurance Law. The findings of
the examination shall be kept in the employer’s records as well as the workers’ files.

articles.label: Article 144
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries > Chapter 4: Medical and Social Services
articles.text:
An employer shall provide his workers with preventive and therapeutic health care in accordance
with the standards set forth by the Minister, taking into consideration whatever is provided for by the
Cooperative Health Insurance Law.

articles.label: Article 145
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries > Chapter 4: Medical and Social Services
articles.text:
An employer may, subject to the Minister’s approval, set up a savings and thrift fund, provided that
the workers’ contribution thereto is optional. The provisions regulating the operation of such funds
shall be made public.

articles.label: Article 146
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries > Chapter 4: Medical and Social Services
articles.text:
An employer shall provide at his own expense all or some of the following, as may be determined by
the Minister, for those who work in remote locations:
1. Stores for selling food, clothing, and other necessities at moderate prices in places where such
stores are not available.
2. Suitable recreational and educational services and sports facilities annexed to the workplace.
3. Necessary medical arrangements to protect the workers’ health and provide comprehensive
treatment for their families (Family shall mean the worker’s spouse, and the children and parents
residing with him).
4. Schools for the workers’ children in the absence of sufficient schools in the area.
5. Mosques or prayer areas at the workplace.
6. Literacy programs for the workers.
The Regulations shall specify remote locations.

articles.label: Article 147
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries > Chapter 4: Medical and Social Services
articles.text:
An employer operating in remote locations, mines, quarries, and oil exploration centers shall provide
his workers with accommodation, camps, and meals.
The Minister shall determine, pursuant to a decision by him, the conditions and specifications of the
accommodation and camps as well as the charges for the accommodation, the number of meals,
quantities and kinds of food and related conditions, cost of meals to the worker, and any other
requirements necessary for the workers’ health.

articles.label: Article 148
articles.chapter: Part 8: Protection Against Occupational Hazards, Major Industrial Accidents and Work > Chapter 1: Protection Against Occupational Hazards > Chapter 2: Protection Against Major Industrial Accidents > Chapter 3: Work Injuries > Chapter 4: Medical and Social Services
articles.text:
An employer shall provide means for transporting his workers from their place of residence or from
a certain gathering point to the places of work and bringing them back daily, if the places of work are
not served by regular means of transportation at times compatible with the working hours.

articles.label: Article 151
articles.chapter: Part 9: Employment of Women
articles.text:
1. A female worker shall be entitled to a fully paid 12-week maternity leave, six weeks of
which must be taken immediately after delivery. The remaining six weeks may be taken at
the worker’s discretion starting four weeks prior to the due date as determined by a medical
report certified by a health institution. If the remainder of the leave is less than six weeks
due to delivery past the due date, the period completing the six-week leave shall be unpaid.
In all cases, the maternity leave may be extended for one month without pay.
2. In the event of giving birth to a sick child or a child with a disability whose health condition
requires constant attendance, a female worker shall be entitled to a one-month leave with
full pay starting at the end of the maternity leave and she shall be entitled to extend the leave
for an additional month as unpaid leave

articles.label: Article 152
articles.chapter: Part 9: Employment of Women
articles.text:
During the maternity leave, an employer shall pay the female worker half her wage if she has been in
his service for one year or more, and a full wage if she has served for three years or more as of the
date of commencement of such leave. A female worker shall not be paid any wages during her regular
annual leave if she has enjoyed in the same year a maternity leave with full wage. She shall be paid
half her wage during the annual leave if she has enjoyed in the same year a maternity leave at half
wage.

articles.label: Article 153
articles.chapter: Part 9: Employment of Women
articles.text: An employer shall provide medical care for female workers during pregnancy and delivery.

articles.label: Article 154
articles.chapter: Part 9: Employment of Women
articles.text:
When a female worker returns to work following a maternity leave, she shall be entitled, in addition
to the rest periods granted to all workers, to a rest period or periods not exceeding in aggregate one
hour a day for nursing her infant. Such period or periods shall be calculated as part of the actual
working hours and shall not entail any reduction in wage.

articles.label: Article 155
articles.chapter: Part 9: Employment of Women
articles.text:
An employer may not terminate the employment of a female worker or give her a warning of
the same during her pregnancy or while she is on maternity leave. This shall include the period
she is ill as a result of either of them, provided that her illness is documented pursuant to an
official medical report, and that her absence does not exceed 180 days a year whether separately
or consecutively

articles.label: Article 157
articles.chapter: Part 9: Employment of Women
articles.text:
A female worker shall forfeit her entitlements under the provisions of this Part if she works for
another employer during her authorized leave. In this case, the original employer may deprive her of
her wage for the duration of the leave or recover any payments made to her.

articles.label: Article 158
articles.chapter: Part 9: Employment of Women
articles.text:
In all occupations and places where women are employed, the employer shall provide them with seats
for resting.

articles.label: Article 159
articles.chapter: Part 9: Employment of Women
articles.text:
1. An employer who employs 50 female workers or more shall provide them with a suitable place
with an adequate number of babysitters to look after the female workers’ children under the age
of six years, if the number of children reaches 10 or more.
2. The Minister may require an employer who employs 100 women or more in a single city to set up
a nursery, either on his own or in conjunction with other employers in the same city, or
alternatively, to contract with an existing nursery to care for the children of the female workers
who are under six years of age during work periods. In such case, the Minister shall set forth the
terms and conditions regulating such facilities as well as the charges imposed on the female
workers benefiting from this service.

articles.label: Article 160
articles.chapter: Part 9: Employment of Women
articles.text:
1. A Muslim female worker whose husband dies shall be entitled to ‘iddah leave’ with full pay
for a period of not less than four months and 10 days starting from date of death. If she is
pregnant, such leave may be extended without pay until her delivery. She may not, following
childbirth, use the remainder of the leave granted to her under this Law.
2. A non-Muslim female worker whose husband dies shall be entitled to a fifteen-day leave
with full pay.
In all cases, a female worker whose husband dies may not work for others during the leave
period.
The employer shall have the right to request supporting documents in the abovementioned
cases

articles.label: Article 161
articles.chapter: Part 10: Employment of Minors
articles.text:
Minors may not be employed in hazardous jobs or harmful industries, or in occupations or jobs that
may endanger their health, safety, or morals due to the nature or conditions of the same. The Minister
shall specify such jobs, industries, and occupations pursuant to a decision issued by him.

articles.label: Article 162
articles.chapter: Part 10: Employment of Minors
articles.text:
1. Any person under the age of 15 years may not be employed or allowed to enter places of work.
The Minister may, pursuant to a decision by him, raise this age limit in certain industries or areas
or for certain categories of minors.
2. As an exception to paragraph (1) of this Article, the Minister may allow the employment or work
of persons between 13 and 15 years of age in light works, subject to the following conditions:
2.1 Such jobs shall not be potentially harmful to their health or growth.
2.2 Such jobs shall not hinder their school attendance or their participation in orientation or
vocational training programs, or impair their ability to benefit from their schooling.

articles.label: Article 163
articles.chapter: Part 10: Employment of Minors
articles.text:
Minors may not work during a period of night the duration of which is not less than 12 consecutive
hours, except in cases determined pursuant to a decision by the Minister.

articles.label: Article 164
articles.chapter: Part 10: Employment of Minors
articles.text:
Minors may not be made to perform actual work for more than six hours a day for all months except
for the month of Ramadan when the actual working hours shall not exceed four hours.
Working hours shall be organized so that a minor does not work for more than four consecutive hours
without one or more periods, each not less than half an hour, for rest, food, and prayers, provided that
the minor does not remain at the workplace for more than seven hours.
Minors may not be made to work during weekly rest days, Eids, official holidays, or annual vacations,
nor shall they be subject to the exceptions provided for in Article 106 of this Law.

articles.label: Article 165
articles.chapter: Part 10: Employment of Minors
articles.text:
Prior to employing a minor, the employer shall obtain from him the following documents:
1. The national identification card or an official birth certificate.
2. A report of physical fitness for the required job issued by a competent physician and duly certified
by a health authority.
3. The consent of the minor’s guardian.
Said documents shall be kept in the minor’s personal file.

articles.label: Article 166
articles.chapter: Part 10: Employment of Minors
articles.text:
An employer shall notify the competent labor office of the employment of each minor within the first
week of such employment, and shall keep at the workplace a register for employed minors, showing
the name of the minor, his age, the full name of his guardian, his place of residence, and the date of
his employment.

articles.label: Article 167
articles.chapter: Part 10: Employment of Minors
articles.text:
The provisions provided for in this Part shall not apply to work undertaken by children and minors in
schools for general, vocational, or technical education, and in other training institutions, nor shall
they apply to work undertaken in establishments by persons who are at least 14 years of age if such
work is performed in accordance with the conditions set forth by the Minister and the work constitutes
an essential part of the following:
1. An educational or training course the primary responsibility for which lies with a school or training
institution.
2. A training program all or the major part of which is implemented in an establishment if approved
by the competent authority.
3. An orientation program aimed at facilitating the selection of the career or type of training.

articles.label: Article 168
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
The words and phrases (vessel, vessel chandler, captain, seafarer, and marine employment
contract) wherever mentioned in this Part shall have the meanings assigned thereto in the
Commercial Maritime Law

articles.label: Article 169
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text: All persons working on a vessel shall be subject to the authority and orders of its captain.

articles.label: Article 170
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
All employment contracts of seamen working on a vessel shall be entered in the vessel’s records or
appended thereto. Such contracts shall be drafted in clear language, and shall indicate whether they
are made for a specific period or for a single voyage. If the contract is made for a specific period, this
period shall be clearly specified. If it is made for a single voyage, it shall specify the city or harbor
where the voyage ends, and at what stage of unloading or loading the vessel at this harbor the contract
terminates.

articles.label: Article 171
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
A marine employment contract shall provide for the date and place of its conclusion, name of the
chandler, name of the seafarer, his surname, age, nationality, and homeland, as well as the type of
assigned work, method of performance, certification for work in sea navigation, personal marine card,
wage, and the duration of the contract. If the contract is for a single voyage, it shall specify the city
or harbor where the voyage ends and at what stage during the unloading or loading of the vessel at
the harbor the work ends, and other details of the contract.
Such contract shall be made out in three copies, one copy for the vessel’s chandler, one for the captain,
to be kept on board the vessel, and a copy for the seafarer.

articles.label: Article 172
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
Work terms and rules aboard the vessel shall be posted in the crew’s quarters. These terms and rules
shall include the following:
1. Seamen’s obligations and duties, organization rules for work aboard the vessel, service timetables,
and daily working hours.
2. Obligations of the vessel’s chandler towards the seamen in respect of fixed wages, rewards, and
other types of wage.
3. Methods of suspending payment of wages and deductions therefrom and methods of advance
payments.
4. Place and time of settlement of wages as well as the final calculation thereof.
5. Rules and ways for the provision of food and accommodation aboard the vessel.
6. Treatment of seamen’s illnesses and injuries.
7. Conduct of seamen and the conditions for their repatriation.
8. Seamen’s paid annual leaves.
9. End-of-service award and other indemnities payable upon termination or expiration of the
employment contract.

articles.label: Article 173
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
A seafarer shall:
1. have completed 18 years of age;
2. hold a certificate allowing him to work in marine service; and
3. be physically fit.

articles.label: Article 174
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
All the seafarer’s entitlements shall be paid in the official currency. They may be paid in foreign
currency if they become due while the vessel is outside territorial waters, subject to the seafarer's
approval.
The seafarer may ask the employer to pay his due monetary wage to the person designated by him.

articles.label: Article 175
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
If the voyage is cut short for any reason, voluntarily or forcibly, this shall not entail a reduction of
the wage of the seafarer employed on a marine employment contract for a single voyage.

articles.label: Article 176
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
If the wage is set as a share of the profits or the proceeds of the vessel's charter, the seafarer shall not
be entitled to compensation if the voyage is cancelled nor to a wage increase if the voyage is delayed
or extended. If the delay or extension is due to the action of the shippers, the seafarer shall be entitled
to compensation from the chandler.

articles.label: Article 177
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
A seafarer shall be eligible for pay, through the day of occurrence, if the ship is captured, sinks, or
becomes unseaworthy.

articles.label: Article 178
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
Without prejudice to the provisions relating to maritime employment contracts provided for
in this Law, regulations governing maritime employment contracts shall be issued pursuant to
a decision by the Minister in coordination with the Transport General Authority. Such
regulations shall include provisions relating to the rights and obligations of the parties to the
contract; living conditions, safety, food, sleeping quarters, and entertainment on board the
vessel; measures to be taken by the employer to prevent occupational injuries and diseases;
health care; working and resting hours and vacations; training seafarer and developing their
skills; repatriation of seamen to their home countries; issuing a certificate indicating the vessel’s
compliance with the provisions of this Law; the mechanism for inspecting and monitoring the
vessel’s compliance with this Law; violations and their prescribed penalties; and amicable
settlement of complaints

articles.label: Article 179
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
Working hours aboard the vessel while on high seas shall not exceed 14 hours in a 24-hour period
and not more than 72 hours in a seven-day period.

articles.label: Article 180
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
A seafarer who contributes to aiding or rescuing another vessel is eligible to a share of the reward
that the vessel on which he works is entitled to, regardless of the type of wage of the work performed.

articles.label: Article 181
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
If a seafarer dies during the voyage, his heirs shall be eligible to receive his wages through the date
of his death, if the wage is on a monthly basis. If the wage is on a voyage basis, the heirs shall be
entitled to the full wage of the voyage, and if the wage is a share of the profits, it shall be fully payable.
The dues of the deceased or missing seafarer, or who is unable to collect his wage shall be deposited
with the labor office at the port of destination in the Kingdom.

articles.label: Article 182
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
An employer may terminate the contract without prior notice and without compensation if the
voyage is cancelled prior to its outset, for reasons beyond the chandler’s control and the wage
is on the basis of a single voyage, unless the contract provides otherwise

articles.label: Article 183
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
If the contract expires or is revoked, the employer shall be obligated to:
1. return the seafarer to the port of departure at the commencement of the contract; and
2. provide him with food and accommodation until he reaches that port.

articles.label: Article 184
articles.chapter: Part 11: Marine Employment Contract
articles.text:
A chandler shall return the seafarer to his country in the following cases:
1. If the chandler cancels the voyage after the vessel sails off.
2. If the voyage is cancelled after the vessel sails off on account of prohibition of trading with the
destination.
3. If the seafarer is removed from the vessel due to illness, injury, or disability.
4. If the vessel is sold in a foreign country.
5. If the seafarer is dismissed from service during the voyage without a legitimate justification.
6. If the contract concluded with the seafarer expires at a port other than the one provided for in the
contract.

articles.label: Article 185
articles.chapter: Part 12: Working in Mines and Quarries
articles.text:
Working in mines and quarries shall mean the following:
1. Operations involving prospecting, detecting, extracting, or manufacturing (solid or liquid) mineral
substances, including precious stones, in the area for which the license was issued.
2. Operations involving extracting, concentrating, or manufacturing mineral sediments on the surface
or under the ground in the area of the license.
3. Construction works and the installation of structures and equipment related to the operations
referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) of this Article.

articles.label: Article 186
articles.chapter: Part 12: Working in Mines and Quarries
articles.text: No person under the age of 18 may be employed in a mine or quarry

articles.label: Article 187
articles.chapter: Part 12: Working in Mines and Quarries
articles.text:
No person shall be allowed to engage in operations subject to the provisions of this Part until he
undergoes a complete medical examination and is proven to be physically fit for the required work.
Such examination shall be repeated periodically. The worker may not be required to bear the costs of
necessary medical examinations. The Minister shall set forth, pursuant to a decision by him, the terms,
conditions, and periods that must be complied with.

articles.label: Article 188
articles.chapter: Part 12: Working in Mines and Quarries
articles.text:
The actual working hours spent by the worker underground shall not exceed seven hours a day. No
worker shall be kept at the workplace, above or below the ground, for more than 10 hours a day. If
the work is conducted underground, such a period shall include the time needed for the worker to
reach underground and the time needed to return to the surface.

articles.label: Article 189
articles.chapter: Part 12: Working in Mines and Quarries
articles.text:
Access to the work location and facilities shall be restricted to workers therein, persons authorized to
inspect the mine or quarry, and persons holding special permits from the competent authority.

articles.label: Article 190
articles.chapter: Part 12: Working in Mines and Quarries
articles.text:
An employer shall keep a record to register and count the workers before they enter the workplace
and as they exit therefrom.

articles.label: Article 191
articles.chapter: Part 12: Working in Mines and Quarries
articles.text:
An employer or the manager in-charge shall draft a list of orders and instructions related to public
safety.

articles.label: Article 192
articles.chapter: Part 12: Working in Mines and Quarries
articles.text:
An employer shall establish a rescue point in the vicinity of the workplace, equipped with necessary
rescue and first aid equipment. Said point shall be equipped with suitable means of communication
for immediate access, and the employer shall appoint a trained technician to supervise rescue and
first aid operations.

articles.label: Article 193
articles.chapter: Part 12: Working in Mines and Quarries
articles.text:
Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 142 of this Law, the employer of each mine or quarry
with at least 50 workers shall set up a suitable location with a room equipped with rescue and first
aid equipment, another room for nursing, and one or more locker rooms. As for quarries and mines
with less than 50 workers and which are located within a twenty-kilometer radius of each other,
employers may pool their resources to establish a place of rescue and first aid in between such
quarries and mines, or else establish their own places of rescue and first aid.
The Minister may determine the rescue and first aid equipment and the protection and prevention
measures in mines and quarries as well as employers’ responsibilities and workers’ rights and duties.

articles.label: Article 194
articles.chapter: Part 13: Work Inspection
articles.text:
Work inspection shall be carried out by inspectors appointed from among the Ministry’s staff
or other Saudis pursuant to a decision by the Minister or his designee. They shall have the
powers provided for in this Law

articles.label: Article 196
articles.chapter: Part 13: Work Inspection
articles.text:
Work inspectors shall undertake the following:
1. Monitoring implementation of the provisions of this Law, its Implementing Regulations, and
the decisions issued in implementation thereof.
2. Providing employers and workers with technical information and instructions that enable
them to follow the best methods for implementing the provisions of this Law.
3. Notifying the concerned officials at the Ministry of the shortcomings of existing provisions,
and submitting relevant proposals.
4. Reporting violations of the provisions of this Law, its Regulations, and the decisions issued
in implementation thereof.
5. Investigating violations which have been detected by other competent government agencies
and referred to the Ministry.
6. Proposing appropriate fines in accordance with the Violations and Penalties Table

articles.label: Article 198
articles.chapter: Part 13: Work Inspection
articles.text:
Work inspectors shall have the right to the following:
1. Access any establishment that is subject to the provisions of the Labor Law at any time during
the working hours of the establishment without prior notice
2. Perform any examination or investigation required to ascertain the proper implementation of the
Law. They may in particular:
a) Question the employer, his representative, or the workers in private or in the presence of
witnesses about any matter relating to the implementation of the provisions of the Law.
b) Review all books, records, and other documents that must be kept pursuant to the provisions of
this Law and relevant decisions, and obtain any copies or extracts therefrom.
c) Take samples of the materials used or handled in industrial and other operations subject to
inspection and believed to have a harmful effect on the health or safety of workers, for the
purpose of analyzing such samples in government laboratories to determine the extent of such
effect, and duly notify the employer or his representative of the same.

articles.label: Article 199
articles.chapter: Part 13: Work Inspection
articles.text:
Employers and their agents and officers at the workplace shall facilitate for the inspectors and officials entrusted with work
inspection the performance of their duties. They shall provide them with the required information
relevant to the nature of their work, respond to requests to appear before them, and dispatch a
representative when asked.

articles.label: Article 200
articles.chapter: Part 13: Work Inspection
articles.text:
A person conducting inspection shall notify the employer or his representative of his visit except
where he believes that the task for which the inspection is being made requires otherwise.

articles.label: Article 201
articles.chapter: Part 13: Work Inspection
articles.text:
A work inspector may instruct employers to amend the rules for operating their equipment and
machinery at deadlines he specifies, to ensure compliance with the provisions pertaining to workers’
health and safety. In the event of a hazard threatening the workers’ health and safety, the inspector
may request the immediate implementation of the measures he deems necessary to prevent such
hazard.

articles.label: Article 202
articles.chapter: Part 13: Work Inspection
articles.text:
A work inspector shall treat with absolute secrecy the complaints he receives regarding any shortage
in equipment or any violation of the provisions of the Law, and he shall not disclose to the employer
or his representative the existence of such complaints.

articles.label: Article 204
articles.chapter: Part 13: Work Inspection
articles.text:
Whenever the need arises, physicians, engineers, chemists, and specialists in occupational health and
safety shall participate in the inspection. If necessary, the director of the labor office and inspectors
may request the competent executive bodies to extend the required assistance.

articles.label: Article 209
articles.chapter: Part 13: Work Inspection
articles.text:
The Minister shall issue the Implementing Regulations necessary for governing and regulating
inspection activities

articles.label: Article 210
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
Commissions for settlement of labor disputes are:
1. The Preliminary Commissions for Settlement of Disputes
2. The High Commission for Settlement of Disputes

articles.label: Article 211
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
Pursuant to a decision by the Minister and following the approval of the President of the Council of
Ministers, members of the preliminary commissions shall be named from among holders of degrees
in Sharia or law.

articles.label: Article 212
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
Based on a decision by the Minister, a preliminary commission comprising one or more one-member
circuits shall be formed in each labor office specified by the Minister. Each of these circuits shall
decide the cases referred to it. If the commission comprises more than one circuit, the Minister shall
name a head from among the members, who shall, in addition to his duties, assign cases to
commission members and organize administrative and clerical work.

articles.label: Article 213
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
If no preliminary commission is formed in a labor office, the Minister shall, when necessary, delegate
the commission formed at the nearest labor office with the duties and jurisdictions of the commission
which has not been formed.

articles.label: Article 214
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
The preliminary commission shall have jurisdiction to:
1. Render final decisions on:
1.1 Labor disputes, irrespective of their type, the value of which does not exceed 10,000 riyals.
1.2 Objections to the penalties imposed by employers upon workers.
1.3 Imposing the punishments provided for in this Law for a violation the punishment of which
does not exceed 5,000 riyals and violations with a combined punishment not exceeding 5,000
riyals.
2. Render preliminary decisions on:
2.1 Labor disputes the value of which exceeds 10,000 riyals.
2.2 Disputes over compensation for work injuries, irrespective of the amount of the compensation.
2.3 Disputes over termination of service.
2.4 Imposing the punishments provided for in this Law for a violation the punishment of which
exceeds 5,000 riyals and violations with a combined punishment exceeding 5,000 riyals.
2.5 Imposing punishments on violations punishable by fines and consequential punishments.

articles.label: Article 215
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
The High Commission for Settlement of Disputes shall be composed of several circuits, each
comprising of not less than three members. The chairman and members of the commission who shall
be holders of degrees in Sharia and law with expertise in labor disputes shall be named pursuant to a
decision of the Council of Ministers, based on a nomination by the Minister. A decision by the
Minister, based on the recommendation of the Chairman of the Commission, shall specify the number
of circuits of the High Commission and their venue jurisdiction. The Chairman of the Commission
shall select the heads of the circuits, assign the duties of each, and supervise all the administrative
functions of the circuits.

articles.label: Article 216
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
Each of the circuits of the High Commission shall have jurisdiction to decide finally and definitively
on all appeals brought before it against decisions of the circuits of preliminary commissions.

articles.label: Article 217
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
Decisions may be appealed within 30 days from the date of utterance of the preliminary circuit’s
decisions made in the presence of the concerned parties and from the date of notification in other
cases.

articles.label: Article 218
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
If the decision of the preliminary circuit is not appealed within the period specified in the previous
Article, the decision shall be deemed final and enforceable. All decisions of the circuits of the High
Commission shall be deemed enforceable from the date of their issuance.

articles.label: Article 219
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
Each of these commissions shall solely have the exclusive right to consider all disputes relating to
this Law and the disputes arising from employment contracts. It may summon any person for
interrogation or assign one of its members to conduct such interrogation. It may also require the
submission of documents and evidence and take any other measures it may deem fit. The commission
shall also have the right to access any premises of the establishment for the purpose of conducting an
investigation and reviewing all the books, records, and documents it deems necessary.

articles.label: Article 220
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
Cases shall be filed through the competent labor office with the preliminary commissions in whose
locality or under whose jurisdiction the place of work falls. Prior to referring the dispute to the
commission, the labor office shall take the necessary measures to settle the dispute amicably. The
Minister shall issue a decision setting forth relevant procedures and rules.

articles.label: Article 221
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text: Cases arising from the provisions of this Law shall be reviewed promptly.

articles.label: Article 222
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
1. No case shall be accepted by the commissions provided for in this Law involving a claim of the
rights provided for in this Law or arising from an employment contract after 12 months have
elapsed after the termination of the employment relation.
2. No case involving a claim of the rights provided for in the previous Labor Law shall be accepted
after 12 months have elapsed following the effective date of this Law.
3. No complaints regarding violations of the provisions of this Law or the regulations and decisions
issued hereunder shall be accepted after 12 months have elapsed following the date of the
occurrence of the violation.

articles.label: Article 223
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
None of the commissions provided for in this Part may abstain from rendering its decision on the
pretext of the absence of applicable provisions in this Law. In such case, the commissions shall resort
to the principles of Sharia, established judicial precedents, norms, and the principles of justice.

articles.label: Article 224
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
Parties to an employment contract may incorporate a clause in the employment contract providing
for the settlement of disputes through arbitration, or said parties may agree to do so after a dispute
arises. In all cases, the provisions of the Arbitration Law and its Implementing Regulations in force
in the Kingdom shall apply.

articles.label: Article 225
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
Neither of the disputing parties may bring the dispute, upon which a final decision has been rendered
by one of the commissions provided for in this Part, before this Commission or other judicial bodies.

articles.label: Article 226
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
During the reconciliation or arbitration proceedings or while the case is under review before one of
the commissions provided for in this Part, the employer may not change the terms of employment
applicable before the initiation of the proceedings in a way that would cause harm to the worker.

articles.label: Article 227
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
The Commission may order the losing party to pay the other party all or part of the costs incurred by
him.

articles.label: Article 228
articles.chapter: Part 14: Commissions for Settlement of Labor Disputes
articles.text:
The Council of Ministers shall issue the regulations for litigation before the commissions for
settlement of labor disputes.

articles.label: Article 229
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text:
1. Without prejudice to any harsher penalty provided for in any other law, any person infringing
upon any of the provisions of this Law, its Regulations, or the decisions issued in
implementation thereof shall be subject to one or more of the following penalties:
a) A fine not exceeding 100,000 riyals.
b) Closure of the establishment for a period not exceeding 30 days.
c) Permanent closure of the establishment.
2. The penalty imposed on the violator may be doubled in the case of repetition.
3. Fines shall be multiplied by the number of persons subject of the violation

articles.label: Article 229 bis
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text: Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 229 of this Law, any person who violates the provisions of Article 30(1) of this Law shall be subject to a fine not less than two hundred thousand riyals (SAR 200,000) and not more than five hundred thousand riyals (SAR 500,000).

articles.label: Article 230
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text:
1. The Ministry may, pursuant to a decision by the Minister or his designee, impose both or either of the two penalties provided for in subparagraphs (a) and (b) of paragraph (1) of Article 229 of this Law, provided that half of the maximum limit set for each of them is not exceeded. The penalty decision may be appealed before the competent administrative court.
2. Pursuant to a decision by the Minister, a table shall be issued listing violations and the corresponding penalties that do not exceed half of the maximum limit of the two penalties provided for in subparagraphs (a) and (b) of paragraph (1) of Article 229 of this Law, taking into account that the fine shall be commensurate with the gravity of the violation.
3. Pursuant to a decision by the Minister, a table shall be issued listing violations whose penalties exceed half of the maximum limit of the two penalties provided for in subparagraphs (a) and (b) of paragraph (1) of Article 229 of this Law. Such table shall also list violations whose penalties are provided for in subparagraph (c) of paragraph (1) of Article 229.
4. If the violation warrants a penalty that exceeds half of the prescribed maximum limit, or if it warrants the permanent closure of the establishment, in accordance with the table provided for in paragraph (3) of this Article, the Ministry shall file a suit before the competent court to review the case and impose the appropriate penalty provided for in Article 229 of this Law.
5. The Ministry and the violator may agree to settle the violation by means of paying the fine assessed by the Ministry, provided that a decision to this effect is issued by the Minister or his designee.

articles.label: Article 231
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text:
The violator is required to rectify the violation within a period specified by the Regulations.
Otherwise, it shall be considered a new violation

articles.label: Article 232
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text:
Fines prescribed under this Law shall be collected in accordance with the procedures for
collecting public funds. Collected amounts shall be deposited with the Human Resources
Development Fund

articles.label: Article 233
articles.text:
The Minister may grant a financial reward of not more than 25% of the amount of the fine
collected to inspectors and others who help in uncovering any of the violations of the provisions
of this Law, its Regulations, and the decisions issued in implementation thereof

articles.label: Article 234
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text:
A. Labor courts may not hear any claim arising from this Law or from an employment contract upon the lapse of 12 months from the date of termination of the employment relation unless the claimant provides justification acceptable to the court or the defendant admits the right subject of the claim.
B. Labor suits shall be expeditiously heard.

articles.label: Article 235
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text: An employer may not, during the hearing of a suit before a labor court, alter employment conditions existing prior to the initiation of proceedings in a manner that undermines the interest of the worker in the suit.

articles.label: Article 236
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text:
Any person who violates the provisions of Chapters 1 and 2 of Part 8 of this Law and the rules issued
in accordance with the provision of Article 121 of this Law shall be subject to a fine of not less than
3,000 riyals and not more than 10,000 riyals for each violation or closing down the establishment for
not more than 30 days or permanently. The fine and the closing down may be combined along with
the elimination of the source of the hazard.

articles.label: Article 237
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text:
Without prejudice to the punishment provided for in other laws applicable to those who obstruct an
official in the course of his duties, violators of the provisions of Article 199 of this Law shall be
subject to a fine of not less than 5,000 riyals and not more than 10,000 riyals.

articles.label: Article 238
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text:
Any employer, project manager or worker who refuses or delays execution of an arbitration award or
a final decision rendered by any of the labor dispute settlement commissions shall be subject to a fine
of not less than 10,000 riyals and not more than 30,000 riyals.

articles.label: Article 239
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text:
A violator of any of the provisions of this Law and the regulations and decisions issued hereunder
shall be subject to a fine of not less than 2,000 riyals and not more than 5,000 riyals, for punishments
not provided for herein.

articles.label: Article 241
articles.chapter: Part 15: Punishments
articles.text:
In all cases, the violator may pay the maximum prescribed fine as provided for in this Part without
resorting to the Commission for Settlement of Labor Disputes.

articles.label: Article 243
articles.chapter: Part 16: Concluding Provisions
articles.text:
The Minister shall issue, within 180 days from this Law’s entry into force, the decisions and
regulations necessary for implementing the provisions thereof. The Implementing Regulations shall
be published in the Official Gazette.

articles.label: Article 244
articles.chapter: Part 16: Concluding Provisions
articles.text:
This Law shall supersede the Labor and Workers’ Law promulgated by Royal Decree No. M/21 dated
6/9/1389H and shall repeal all the provisions that are inconsistent therewith. Regulations and
decisions issued prior to the effective date of this Law shall remain in effect until they are amended.

articles.label: Article 245
articles.chapter: Part 16: Concluding Provisions
articles.text:
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force 180 days after the date
of its publication.
